18.purpose: Work exploration aims to help people discover suitable work through direct experience and local networks.
18.redlandsAdaptation: A Redlands programme would offer short tasters across trades, care, arts, technology, food growing and repair. Recognised placement arrangements would connect interested people with paid training or employment pathways.
18.conflictBoundary: Luke's work-exploration tools or host role would be relevant to an interest assessment if council funded placements, procured programme support or selected a delivery partner involving him.

19.purpose: Collaborative activities across generations aim to support youth safety and opportunity through trusted relationships and practical learning.
19.redlandsAdaptation: Cooperative puzzles and making challenges could be adapted for libraries, schools and community centres. Optional voice reflection would allow participants and facilitators to explore whether it helps people learn teamwork.
19.mayoralCouncilLever: Council could consider suitable venues and youth, library or arts partnerships for collaborative escape-room sessions and intergenerational making, with community input into the activities.
19.conflictBoundary: Luke's game design, recording tools or delivery role would be relevant to an interest assessment if council commissioned sessions, licensed the format or funded a host involving him.

20.purpose: 500 Queens aims to create opportunities for emerging female leaders to practise long-range civic decision-making and build networks.
20.redlandsAdaptation: Leadership exercises could be adapted to local long-term planning, with human mentors invited through Brisbane, Logan, Toowoomba, Gold Coast, Moreton Bay, Sunshine Coast and other interested councils.
20.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could invite neighbouring councils to a shared leadership and mentoring programme, with each council choosing its contribution.
20.outside: Human mentors and other councils agree their own participation; the mayor cannot appoint them or commit their resources.
20.conflictBoundary: Luke's mentoring, programme or partner role would be relevant to an interest assessment if council funded the network, selected its partners or supported an organisation he joined.

21.purpose: The proposal aims to connect Redlands people and organisations with Brisbane 2032 opportunities and enduring local benefits.
21.redlandsAdaptation: A Redlands participation and legacy discussion with the responsible Games and state bodies would cover accessible visitor information, volunteer and paid-work pathways, local arts and enterprise, and capabilities useful beyond the event. Each independent project would identify its specific Games-related connections.
21.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could represent a council-endorsed Redlands position in regional, state and Games discussions, connect local organisations with the responsible programme owners, and seek clear local-benefit and access arrangements.
21.conflictBoundary: Any personal or business interest Luke has in a Games-related sponsorship, paid role, supplier arrangement or council-supported activity would need to be identified.

22.purpose: Dig for Redlands and Shared Table aim to increase access to healthy local produce and test reductions in household food costs.
22.redlandsAdaptation: Dig for Australia-style growing could be adapted to sunny balconies, fences, yards, schools and suitable shared land in Redlands. Local crop guidance, seed and seedling swaps, and optional produce-sharing circles would support participation.
22.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could convene growers and willing hosts and seek council support for food-growing information, suitable access to council land or venues, and transparent community grant opportunities.
22.conflictBoundary: Seed, equipment, land-access and grant decisions would need transparent processes. Any specific council benefit to Luke, Strange But True or an organisation he joined would require independent handling.

23.purpose: Tip Loop aims to keep useful goods in circulation and reduce replacement costs and waste.
23.redlandsAdaptation: A safe collection route before disposal would include sorting, storage, repair triage and affordable distribution. Interested sheds, makers and existing reuse operators could participate in developing the arrangements.
23.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could bring council waste teams, existing reuse operators, sheds and repairers together around pre-disposal collection, space, storage and distribution arrangements.
23.conflictBoundary: Access to council waste streams, land, grants or contracts would need independent assessment where Luke or a future co-operative had an interest. Allocation and redistribution arrangements would be published.

24.purpose: Shared practical tools and facilities aim to avoid unnecessary individual purchases and connect practical skills with repairs, gardens and learning.
24.redlandsAdaptation: A map of existing makerspaces, sheds and community equipment would inform shared access, maintenance and skills sessions developed with willing hosts across divisions.
24.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for shared facilities, equipment access and practical learning through libraries, venues and community partnerships.
24.conflictBoundary: Access and equipment purchases would need transparent arrangements. Council support involving Luke's equipment, designs, business or an organisation he joined would require independent handling.

25.purpose: Verse Box stations and supported sessions would provide accessible public access for useful personal, creative and community work.
25.redlandsAdaptation: Verse Box stations could be installed and operated with willing libraries and community hosts, with agreed purposes, equipment, accessibility, support, maintenance and session arrangements. Demonstrations would use sample records; personal sessions would provide private handover, export and deletion.
25.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could convene suitable hosts and support council consideration of stations, public access and assistance within its venues or programmes.
25.conflictBoundary: Luke's station design, software or Strange But True would be relevant to an interest assessment if council purchased, licensed, hosted or funded a Verse Box installation.

26.purpose: Local arts, music and cinema participation would create learning and creative opportunities and test affordable cultural activities.
26.redlandsAdaptation: Music, film, making and cultural events could be adapted for willing mainland and island venues, with clear rights, cultural governance and accessible participation.
26.mayoralCouncilLever: Council could support access to its arts venues, libraries, events and relevant community funding pathways for local music, cinema and creative participation.
26.conflictBoundary: Luke's music, creative work or production role would be relevant to an interest assessment if council funded an event, licensed content or commissioned work involving him.

27.purpose: Community noticeboards and locally governed websites aim to make local information easier to find and reduce reliance on commercial social platforms.
27.redlandsAdaptation: A pilot would combine accessible public digital noticeboards with a low-bandwidth website and optional subscriptions for local activities, services and preparedness information.
27.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council support for accessible public information channels and community publishing partnerships, with clear editorial and moderation responsibilities.
27.conflictBoundary: Publishing, moderation and venue access would operate under transparent terms. Any council purchase of Luke's website or noticeboard systems would require independent handling.

28.purpose: Disaster-ready kiosks aim to improve access to reliable information during outages and everyday preparedness.
28.redlandsAdaptation: Site assessment and a pilot would cover offline-capable information, backup power and connectivity, and accessible preparedness material connected to authorised warning and update workflows.
28.mayoralCouncilLever: Council's disaster responsibilities and the Local Disaster Management Group provide the route for integrating kiosks with approved information workflows.
28.conflictBoundary: Kiosk sites, equipment and support contracts would need independent assessment where Luke's designs or equipment could benefit. Responsibilities for publishing authorised warnings would remain clear.

29.purpose: Preparedness and recovery coordination aims to help communities prepare for outages, disrupted transport, heat and recovery needs.
29.redlandsAdaptation: A map of existing resilience assets and gaps would support consented household preparedness assistance, exercises and a register of recovery obligations and resources.
29.mayoralCouncilLever: Existing Local Disaster Management Group and recovery arrangements provide the route for strengthening preparedness, information and handovers.
29.conflictBoundary: Community participation and support records would remain within consented operational arrangements. Any council recovery contract involving Luke or an organisation he joined would require independent assessment.

30.purpose: The proposal explores safe additional housing while permanent construction proceeds.
30.redlandsAdaptation: A review of zoning and existing pathways would compare secondary dwellings, approved temporary homes and serviced modular or kit options. It would identify candidate sites, servicing requirements, costs and pathways for demonstrations or rule changes.

31.purpose: The proposal aims to protect transport choice and examine effects on affordability, frequency and reliability.
31.redlandsAdaptation: The council position, state project documents and access proposals would inform advocacy for transparent multi-operator access, disability access, resilience and consultation on service changes.
31.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek and advocate a council position protecting independent operator access, choice, accessibility and service continuity.
31.conflictBoundary: Luke's personal advocacy would remain distinct from the council position. Any council decision involving a transport operator, supplier or property interest connected to him would require independent handling.

32.purpose: The proposal examines whether underground roads could reduce surface impacts and improve access.
32.redlandsAdaptation: A scoped options study for Minjerribah underground roads would compare them with surface improvements, public transport and a lower level of infrastructure development.
32.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek a council position and scoped engineering work on Minjerribah road access, council road responsibilities and land interfaces, and convene the responsible landholders and transport authorities.
32.conflictBoundary: Any council-funded road study, design licence, land arrangement or tunnelling contract involving Luke's Sandworm intellectual property, business or future delivery interest would require independent handling.

33.purpose: The proposal investigates less disruptive and potentially useful ways to add services without joining the Southern Moreton Bay Islands.
33.redlandsAdaptation: Assessment of smaller tunnelling systems would consider particular sewerage or service alignments on individual islands, alongside trenchless alternatives, conventional works and decentralised services.
33.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could seek council water, wastewater and infrastructure input on specific island service needs and alignments, and convene the responsible service owners and tunnelling partners.

34.title: Spoil reuse, erosion protection and reefs
34.purpose: The proposal explores beneficial reuse and ecological and coastal outcomes where materials and sites are suitable.
34.redlandsAdaptation: Excavated materials and each proposed destination would be assessed separately for lawful reuse, coastal protection and engineered artificial reefs, with nature-based and other options included in the comparison.
34.mayoralCouncilLever: The mayor could convene council coastal and environment teams, custodians and research partners around material testing and identified coastal or reef applications within the relevant council responsibilities.
34.conflictBoundary: Any council material-transfer, testing, coastal-work or reef contract would need independent assessment where Luke had an interest in the excavated material, design or receiving project.
